# Muki's Daily Digest - Research Stage Evidence Dossier (Issue 058)

The following evidence dossier presents the five strongest cultural signals identified within the requested time frame (past 24 hours to 7 days), filtered specifically for Muki’s curatorial, feminist, archival, and creative tech research parameters. 

---

### Section 1: Feminist Structure Signal (Feminist Visual Culture / Labor / Care / Bodies)

*   **Exact Title**: Generative Disruption: Feminist Art from the Collection
*   **Institution/Organizer**: Ruby City (Linda Pace Foundation), San Antonio, Texas, USA
*   **Curator**: Elyse A. Gonzales (Ruby City Director)
*   **Specific Source URL**: [https://rubycity.org/exhibitions/generative-disruption-feminist-art-from-the-collection/](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG4n_Jo4jr_u3k8s3EluMQ68CdEHzYyO0KChPPGJmTiIoqfEExOLznMxcBE0baTEZ3zoakRv0ZZmP_x4E1KojzsH5YBTWmsvKzWLTEOLafz2l3y5z4OL90laiS58Y260h5Ez0jh3N4J62Gx04u-MHZhGN8MJLLGwq-PlcspH_vV6xKCzR4j0634cHdK88wL)
*   **Publication/Exhibition Dates**: September 26, 2026 – August 29, 2027 (Walkthrough & Opening Reception: September 26, 2026)
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   The exhibition draws largely from the Linda Pace Foundation Collection to explore how the ideas of 1960s and 1970s feminist artists continue to shape contemporary art from the 1990s to today.
    *   It centers on domesticity, identity, care, memory, and the reclamation of "lesser" materials historically associated with women's work (fiber, textiles, found objects, ceramics, embroidery, and early non-canonized video art).
    *   Featured artists include Miwa Yanagi (showing *Yuka* from the *My Grandmothers* series, 2000), Laura Aguilar, Nicole Eisenman, Wangechi Mutu, Sue Williams, Nao Bustamante, Mona Hatoum, and Sama Alshaibi.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: It directly aligns with Muki's focus on feminist curating, labor, care, and the historical reclamation of materials and media. By staging works from 1990 to 2026 against 70s feminist thought, it maps the evolution of how "women's labor" and bodily autonomy are visualized.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. No previous mention of this exhibition, Ruby City, or this curatorial project in recent issues.

### Section 2: Visual Culture Signal (Photography / Exhibitions / Photobooks / Curatorial)

*   **Exact Title**: GLUE Book Fair 2026 & "Jesse Glazzard: The Sound of Dirt and Beauty" Exhibition
*   **Institution/Organizer**: Institute of Contemporary Arts (ICA), London, UK
*   **Specific Source URL**: [https://ica.art/bulletin/glue-book-fair-2026](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGZE93__ga21fFwMaip1D98CMJmIOPb25v2DDQ9Gg1T9af0wfx-5eDByw8XjtEIru6nPaq07O-3Exq4hueI-7BIs2jq4wjuSY7bEaSr59L7) *(Note: URL mapped from verification data)*
*   **Publication/Event Dates**: Book Fair: September 12–13, 2026; Exhibition: September 12–20, 2026
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   ICA's annual book fair, GLUE Book Fair, returns with over 90 independent and artist-led publishers to celebrate creative publishing networks.
    *   The event hosts the launch of photographer Jesse Glazzard's new photobook published by *Self Publish, Be Happy (SPBH)*.
    *   Accompanying the launch is Glazzard's solo exhibition, *The Sound of Dirt and Beauty*, which structurally reimagines the traditional "family album" through lenses of queer intimacy, community networks, and the concept of the "living archive".
    *   The program includes hands-on workshops led by Ibrahim Azab, Kairo Urovi, and Eva Jonas.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: Merges photographic exhibition, photobook publishing structures, and the subversion of vernacular family archives. The concept of the "living archive" to explore identity directly connects to Muki's image history and media archaeology interests.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. Neither Jesse Glazzard, SPBH's new launch, nor GLUE Book Fair has been featured in recent issues.

### Section 3: China / East Asia Signal (China / East Asia Photography & Contemporary Art)

*   **Exact Title**: MOT Collection: Past Light, Present Sight
*   **Institution/Organizer**: Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT), Japan
*   **Specific Source URL**: [https://www.mot-art-museum.jp/en/exhibitions/mot-collection-past-light-present-sight/](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEq4UUUKeCbxPqCZlrTg2AujwZ9KNgwBxDOAMHRnpg4Bv4DFN9prBpVWE8sashWLAukN6cEo9h91mmTZyYJQTgMmoMMyrsg1Wl4sxHM9O0Jp5oqRnPGKGdd535GWol8pKKyTYjqUxwgL4Riorea0E4Wx2dYLvlLYoRk) *(Note: URL mapped from verification data)*
*   **Publication/Exhibition Dates**: September 19, 2026 – January 6, 2027
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   The Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT) is presenting its latest collection exhibition, focusing on how "light" and "time" serve as layered traces of memory and history in East Asian post-war art.
    *   The exhibition heavily features newly acquired works by female and contemporary artists, including Mami Kosemura (showing *Flowing Plants of the Four Seasons*), Kimio Tsuchiya (*Absence*), Arisa Kumagai (*Say yes to me*), Shigeo Toya, Hiroshi Sugimoto, and Yayoi Kusama.
    *   The curatorial theme explores the stratification of history, examining how the "now" is constructed by the overlaying of light—from celestial/stellar light to artificial electrical illumination.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: East Asian media archaeology and collection analysis. It demonstrates a curatorial methodology that uses "light" as a physical, indexical, and historical medium to unpack collective memory, especially highlighting under-studied female artists like Mami Kosemura and Arisa Kumagai within the museum's permanent collection.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. While MOT's "Synchronic Constellation" was covered on September 7, this is a completely separate newly curated *MOT Collection* exhibition focusing on different postwar acquisitions and artists.

### Section 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal (AI Workflows / Video Generation Architecture)

*   **Exact Title**: OpenVDN's Video DeltaNet (VDN-H3) Hybrid Attention Checkpoint Released for MiniMax H3
*   **Institution/Developers**: Research team from UC Berkeley, UT Austin, and Impossible, Inc.
*   **Specific Source URL**: [https://s.comfyui-wiki.com/news/2026-09-04-vdn-h3/](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEdi79-HQRET4ihg8J9Np351A0ZBZHBiZ28ol1v_6OZ_gWBtgMnhYM-2gF4tHSYlyX1l_KUDZ__T3ASkeMQs8KruV6MogfK7sWM13o7CBHBiCkJ464ug55dDJRoazkx-TVMbYQmUxdUAA==) *(Note: URL mapped from verification data)*
*   **Publication Date**: September 2, 2026
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   The VDN-H3 checkpoint implements a hybrid-attention rework of MiniMax H3. By replacing the model's dense quadratic long-range attention with a linear "Video Delta Attention" branch, it dramatically lowers computational overhead.
    *   The team has released 8-step and 50-step distilled checkpoints that function as patches on top of the unmodified dense H3 backbone, reporting near-lossless generation quality.
    *   The 8-step model generates a 14.4-second 768p video clip faster than its actual playback time on standard consumer hardware.
    *   A native community-developed ComfyUI node (`Saganaki22/ComfyUI-VDN-H3`) has been released, enabling creators to apply these checkpoints directly to native MiniMax-H3 nodes as runtime model patches.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: Highly material workflow optimization. For independent artists and researchers utilizing local AI video generation, the bottleneck has always been dense attention's quadratic VRAM and speed scaling. VDN-H3 proves that linear-attention approximations can bring "faster-than-playback" generation to consumer-grade local hardware.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: **Follow-up / Ongoing**. This is a direct architectural and performance upgrade to our previous coverage of MiniMax H3 tools (such as the TimelineDirector on Sep 7 and the Sound Sync Challenge on Sep 4). It indicates the rapid maturation of the H3 local open-source ecosystem.

### Section 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity (Grants / Residencies / Open Calls)

*   **Exact Title**: Open Call: Singapore Art Museum (SAM) Residencies Cycle 4 (2027/2028)
*   **Institution/Organizer**: Singapore Art Museum (SAM), Singapore
*   **Specific Source URL**: [https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/615822/residencies-cycle-4-2027-2028/](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEMnHn2u33EOC9dVR_2mQfAHJGGX2AgTTW13hjSFVFxSdaKBHcKSY8BnWBjBYv4Xy3XAfzo9YAT9402s61LmxztzPF312OfCHmsgEUBKp_PcCRVV8v_HIt-Uqrk4CNMysUyYfVJvDWAih254FuEaMwYJUkxHygHhIG7PjKFcaEp02A5QWiiTCWp2LQvJds=) *(Note: URL mapped from verification data)*
*   **Deadline**: September 30, 2026 (11:59 PM GMT+8)
*   **Verified Facts**:
    *   SAM has opened applications for Cycle 4 of its international residency program, scheduled to run from June 2027 to December 2028 at its post-industrial warehouse spaces in Tanjong Pagar Distripark, Singapore.
    *   The open call is open to global artists, curators, educators, researchers, and creative practitioners across three specific strands:
        1.  *Listening/Attuning*: Practices responding critically to the sociopolitical urgencies of our time.
        2.  *Making/Material Cultures*: Material inquiry and the tangible processes of making.
        3.  *Beyond Human/Interdependence*: Investigating relationships between humans, technologies, ecologies, and other life forms.
    *   The program provides dedicated studio spaces, research resources, institutional networking, and supports open studios, screenings, workshops, and talks.
*   **Relevance to Muki**: This is a premier East Asian institutional residency that aligns deeply with Muki's interest in the intersection of material cultures, critical tech (Beyond Human), and post-colonial/ecological care. It is a high-value, fully supported research opportunity for independent curators and visual researchers.
*   **Duplication Assessment**: **New**. This is the launch of Cycle 4 of SAM Residencies; no previous cycles have been featured in recent issues.
